scenes.line1: How do big apps handle tons of users?
scenes.say: How do huge web apps stay fast and reliable, even with millions of users? What's the secret to scaling out?

scenes.label: Balancer
scenes.sub: Distributes requests across servers for reliability.
scenes.say: A load balancer sits in front of your servers. It spreads incoming requests across multiple machines, keeping things reliable and smooth.
Stateless services don't keep user data between requests. That means you can add more servers whenever you need, making it easy to scale horizontally.
Stateful services remember users, which makes scaling tough. Stateless services forget everything—so you can add or remove servers without hassle.

scenes.question: Can you store sessions on the server?
scenes.right: No. Storing sessions breaks statelessness and limits scaling.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: Can you store sessions on the server? No! That breaks statelessness and kills your ability to scale easily.
